headline: Record profit, expanding margins, growing customer base
summary_short: Nu Holdings posted its first-ever $1 billion+ quarterly net income at $1,061.1M (+17% q/q, +49% y/y) as revenue rose 6% q/q to $5,875.7M, with net interest margin expanding 180bps to 22.9% and total customers reaching 138.9 million.
summary_long: Revenue climbed to $5,875.7M (managerial basis, +6% q/q FXN) as NII grew 9% q/q on portfolio growth and a mix shift toward unsecured lending; risk-adjusted NIM expanded 290bps to 12.4% as cost of credit fell 9% q/q on seasonal delinquency improvement. Gross profit rose 25% q/q to $2,441.1M and net income hit a record $1,061.1M (ROE 33%), even as the efficiency ratio rose to 19.5% on real-estate and marketing spend shifting into the quarter plus international-expansion investment. Credit portfolio grew 5% q/q to $39.4B and deposits rebounded 6% q/q to $45.3B after Q1's seasonal outflows. Customers reached 138.9 million, with Mexico completing its shift to a full-scale bank in August. No numeric forward guidance was given.

drivers.explanation: CEO cited crossing $1B in quarterly net income, the August launch of Nu's bank in Mexico, a new full banking license in Brazil, launch of Croma for Super Core customers, and NuFormer's expanding role in underwriting and service.
Growth reflects NII up 9% q/q from portfolio growth and a mix shift toward unsecured lending plus intentional risk expansion communicated the prior quarter.
Record net income driven by gross profit growth outpacing operating expense growth, with credit's contribution to gross profit normalizing to 41% on its expected seasonal pattern.
Reflects revenue growth combined with cost of credit falling 9% q/q on normal second-quarter improvement in early delinquencies.
Expansion reflects portfolio growth, mix shift toward unsecured lending, and the intentional risk expansions the company flagged last quarter.
NIM expansion combined with a 9% q/q decline in cost of credit from seasonal delinquency improvement drove the 290bps gain.
Ratio rose (efficiency worsened) as real estate and marketing expenses shifted from Q1 into Q2, alongside continued investment in international expansion.
Improvement mostly reflects seasonality, partially offset by intentional expansion into higher-risk, higher-return segments; product mix effects were broadly neutral.
Increase largely reflects the seasonal migration of first-quarter early delinquencies into the 90+ bucket.
Added roughly 4 million customers in the quarter across Brazil (~118M), Mexico (15.8M), and Colombia (5M+), continuing steady net additions.
Growth spans credit cards ($26B), unsecured lending ($10.3B), and secured lending ($3.1B); not decomposed further by the company for the quarter's growth specifically.
Recovery from Q1's seasonal outflows, led by Brazil ($36.4B); Mexico deposits declined modestly again as part of a deliberate deposit-optimization strategy that improved funding cost.
